strategies.name: breadth_risk_switch
strategies.rationale: Market breadth as a regime signal: when most sectors trade above their long-run average, the advance is broad and drawdown risk is low; narrowing breadth tends to precede bear markets (Zweig; Faber). Long SPY when the share of sectors above their moving average exceeds a threshold, flat otherwise. Weekly.
strategies.failure_condition: Sharpe not above the plain SPY 200dma trend benchmark, or the filter misses recoveries badly enough that CAGR is < half buy-and-hold.
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: dual_momentum_regions
strategies.rationale: Antonacci-style dual momentum: relative momentum picks the strongest of US, developed ex-US and EM equity; absolute (time-series) momentum moves to cash when even the winner's trailing return is negative, sidestepping prolonged bear markets.
strategies.failure_condition: Sharpe not above buy-and-hold SPY in-sample, or whipsaw losses around V-shaped recoveries (2020-style) exceeding the drawdown it avoids.
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: factor_momentum_rotation
strategies.rationale: Factor momentum (Ehsani-Linnainmaa 2022; Gupta-Kelly 2019): equity factors' own returns are autocorrelated. Rank MTUM/QUAL/USMV/VLUE by trailing return in excess of SPY, long the leader, short SPY against it to isolate the factor spread from market beta. Monthly.
strategies.failure_condition: Excess-of-SPY spread has Sharpe < 0.3, or the book is dominated by noise because factor ETFs share >90% of variance with SPY.
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: index_tsmom
strategies.rationale: Time-series momentum (Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen 2012): each equity index's own trailing return predicts its next-month sign, driven by under-reaction then delayed over-reaction. Long/short each of SPY/QQQ/IWM/EFA/EEM by the sign of its trailing return, inverse-vol weighted. Monthly.
strategies.failure_condition: Sharpe < 0.3 or losses concentrated in sharp reversals (2009, 2020) that exceed the crisis-alpha gains; high correlation (>0.85) with the breadth/trend strategies would also make it redundant.
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: sector_low_vol_bab
strategies.rationale: Betting-against-beta / low-vol anomaly (Frazzini-Pedersen 2014): leverage-constrained investors overpay for high-beta assets. Long the lowest-beta sectors and short the highest-beta sectors, each leg scaled by 1/beta so the book is approximately beta neutral to SPY. Monthly.
strategies.failure_condition: Sharpe < 0.3 in-sample, or P&L reduces to a disguised short-tech/long-utilities rate bet that loses in every equity rally.
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: sector_momentum_12_1
strategies.rationale: Industry momentum (Moskowitz-Grinblatt 1999): sectors with strong trailing 12-month returns, skipping the most recent month to avoid short-term reversal, keep outperforming as information diffuses slowly across industries. Long top-n sectors, short bottom-n, dollar neutral, monthly.
strategies.failure_condition: Net in-sample Sharpe < 0.3 or a rolling 3-year Sharpe below zero for most of the post-2009 period (momentum crashes dominate the premium).
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: sector_short_reversal
strategies.rationale: Short-horizon reversal (Lehmann 1990; Jegadeesh 1990) from liquidity provision: sectors that over/under-shot last week due to flow pressure tend to mean-revert. Long the weakest sectors, short the strongest, rebalanced weekly.
strategies.failure_condition: Gross edge is too small to survive 5bp costs at weekly turnover (net Sharpe < 0.3), or returns concentrate in 2008-09 only.
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: spy_trend_benchmark
strategies.rationale: Benchmark: hold SPY when above its 200-day average (time-series momentum).
strategies.failure_condition: Sharpe below buy-and-hold SPY over a full cycle.
strategies.author: framework

strategies.name: credit_regime_duration
strategies.rationale: Credit leads rates: when high-yield underperforms Treasuries (HYG/IEF falling, spreads widening) growth expectations are deteriorating and a flight-to-quality bid lifts duration; when credit outperforms, carry in HY dominates and duration lags. Long TLT/IEF in stress regimes, long HYG in benign regimes. LQD/IEF used before HYG exists.
strategies.failure_condition: Sharpe < 0.3, or the regime signal fails in inflation-driven selloffs where credit and duration fall together (2022), producing losses on both legs.
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: duration_momentum
strategies.rationale: Rate cycles are persistent because central banks move in long, telegraphed cycles: when long duration has out-returned the front end over the trailing window, stay long duration (TLT), short when the front end has out-returned it; SHY is used only as the signal benchmark. Captures easing/tightening cycles and bull/bear steepeners.
strategies.failure_condition: Sharpe < 0.3, or losses concentrated in sharp policy pivots (2013 taper tantrum, 2022), or performance indistinguishable from simply holding TLT.
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: fx_trend
strategies.rationale: Currency trend: FX moves are driven by persistent policy-rate and growth divergences that central banks change gradually, so exchange-rate trends persist. Moving-average-crossover or return-sign signal per G10 pair, inverse-vol weighted.
strategies.failure_condition: Sharpe < 0.2 in-sample, or edge disappears post-2012 (known decay of FX trend as rates converged to zero), or performance relies on a single pair.
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: gold_real_rates
strategies.rationale: Gold is a zero-coupon real asset; its opportunity cost is the real yield. Falling real yields (TIP rallying) or rising breakevens (TIP outperforming IEF) are bullish for gold and silver, rising real yields bearish. Trade GLD (and SLV) long/short on the trailing change in the real-rate / breakeven proxy.
strategies.failure_condition: Sharpe < 0.3, or the gold/real-rate link breaks (as in 2022-24 when central-bank buying kept gold rising despite surging real yields), or no better than GLD trend alone.
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: risk_parity_trend
strategies.rationale: Long-only inverse-vol risk parity across duration, credit, inflation-linked, gold and commodities earns diversified risk premia; a moving-average filter drops assets in downtrends (Faber-style) to cut the deep drawdowns that sink plain risk parity (2008, 2022).
strategies.failure_condition: Sharpe below unfiltered inverse-vol portfolio, or max DD > 25% (2.5x sleeve limit), or whipsaw costs consume the drawdown savings.
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: ts_trend_multi
strategies.rationale: Time-series momentum across bonds, commodities and FX (Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen): slow-moving macro information and investor under-reaction make trailing returns predict next-month returns. Inverse-vol sizing, blended lookbacks, sign signals.
strategies.failure_condition: In-sample Sharpe < 0.3, or rolling 3y Sharpe negative in more than 40% of windows, or losses concentrated in trend reversals with no crisis payoff (2008).
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: xasset_momentum_rank
strategies.rationale: Cross-sectional momentum across macro assets (Asness-Moskowitz-Pedersen 'value and momentum everywhere'): rank risk-adjusted 12-1 / 6-1 month returns, long the top k, short the bottom k. Captures relative capital flows between asset classes.
strategies.failure_condition: Sharpe < 0.3, or long and short legs both lose (signal noise), or monthly momentum crashes dominate drawdowns (e.g. 2009 reversals).
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: ts_carry_svxy
strategies.rationale: Short-dated VIX futures roll down a contango curve, so short-VIX ETFs earn a roll yield / insurance premium; harvest it only when VIX/VIX3M is clearly below 1 and step aside to SHY when the curve flattens or inverts, which historically precedes or coincides with vol spikes.
strategies.failure_condition: In-sample Sharpe < 0.5, or max drawdown worse than 2x the 8% sleeve budget, or a single-day loss > 5% after vol targeting (i.e. the curve filter fails to get us out before a spike like Feb 2018 / Mar 2020).
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: ts_regime_hedge
strategies.rationale: An inverted VIX curve (VIX > VIX3M) marks acute stress in which equities have negative drift and duration / long-vol rally. Hold SPY in contango; switch to TLT plus a small long-VIX (VIXY) sleeve in backwardation to convert crisis convexity into return. VIXY is only held while inverted because it decays heavily in contango.
strategies.failure_condition: Sharpe < 0.5, or whipsaw costs around ratio ~1 dominating, or the VIXY leg having negative contribution in stress episodes.
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: vix_spike_reversion
strategies.rationale: Fear spikes overshoot: forced deleveraging and hedging demand push VIX far above its recent norm, after which VIX mean-reverts and equities rebound. Buy SPY once a spike (VIX z-score vs trailing 60d) has peaked and VIX has begun to fall, hold for a fixed horizon, otherwise sit in SHY.
strategies.failure_condition: Sharpe < 0.5, or most of the PnL coming from a single episode, or losses concentrated in prolonged bear markets (2008) where spikes keep re-occurring.
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: vol_managed_spy
strategies.rationale: Equity volatility is persistent but its expected return is not proportional, so scaling SPY exposure by inverse recent variance raises Sharpe and, by cutting exposure as vol clusters, shortens drawdowns. Residual cash in SHY.
strategies.failure_condition: Sharpe not above unmanaged SPY over the same window, or drawdown worse than 16% (scaling reacts too slowly to gap-down crashes).
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: vrp_carry_svxy
strategies.rationale: Short-vol carry pays when two independent premia agree: the futures curve is in contango (roll yield) and implied vol exceeds realised vol (insurance premium). Requiring both, plus VIX not in an uptrend vs its 10d mean, should cut exposure ahead of vol shocks more reliably than either signal alone.
strategies.failure_condition: Not improving drawdown vs ts_carry_svxy, Sharpe < 0.5, or correlation > 0.85 with ts_carry_svxy (redundant).
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: vrp_spy_timing
strategies.rationale: When implied vol (VIX) sits well above trailing realised SPY vol, option sellers are being paid a large insurance premium and forward equity returns per unit risk are higher; when realised exceeds implied (negative VRP) the market is in a disorderly regime, so hold Treasuries instead.
strategies.failure_condition: Sharpe < 0.5 or not better than a SPY 200d-trend benchmark on a risk-adjusted basis; drawdown worse than 16%.
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: btc_eth_rotation
strategies.rationale: The two deepest, most liquid coins alternate leadership (ETH outperforms in risk-on/DeFi phases, BTC in flight-to-quality). Hold the one with stronger trailing return, only if its own trailing return is positive; else flat.
strategies.failure_condition: Sharpe below a static 50/50 BTC/ETH trend-filtered basket, i.e. the relative-strength leg adds nothing beyond absolute trend.
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: btc_trend_ensemble
strategies.rationale: Time-series momentum in BTC: crypto flows are reflexive (rising prices attract retail/leverage inflows), so trailing returns over several horizons predict the next weeks' drift. Exposure = fraction of lookbacks with positive return.
strategies.failure_condition: Sharpe below buy-and-hold BTC over a full cycle, or repeated whipsaw losses in range-bound regimes (e.g. 2019, 2022 H2) exceeding the 20% DD budget.
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: donchian_breakout
strategies.rationale: Crypto rallies start with range breakouts that trigger momentum/short-covering cascades. Enter a coin on a close at its N-day high, exit on a close at its N/2-day low (classic turtle). Applied to BTC, ETH, LTC (longest, deepest history).
strategies.failure_condition: False breakouts dominate (hit rate too low to cover 15 bps costs), or Sharpe no better than the simpler BTC moving-average trend.
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: invvol_trend_basket
strategies.rationale: Diversified exposure to the crypto beta while sidestepping deep bear markets: each eligible coin is held only above its own moving average, sized by inverse trailing vol so DOGE/SOL do not dominate risk.
strategies.failure_condition: Diversification fails (coin correlations -> 1 in crashes) so drawdowns match BTC trend with lower Sharpe; or MA exits lag so DD > 20%.
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: st_reversal_uptrend
strategies.rationale: Liquidity provision: over 1-2 weeks, coins that sold off hardest relative to peers (forced liquidations, leverage flushes) tend to mean-revert. Buy the bottom-k weekly losers among eligible coins, only while BTC is in an uptrend.
strategies.failure_condition: Losers keep losing (momentum dominates at weekly horizon) so the strategy underperforms the equal-weight eligible basket under the same BTC filter.
strategies.author: research-agent

strategies.name: xs_momentum_btc_regime
strategies.rationale: Cross-sectional momentum: capital rotates into the coins with the strongest narratives and liquidity; winners keep winning over 1-3 months. Only active when BTC is above its 100d average, since alt-coins crash together in bear markets.
strategies.failure_condition: Top-k basket fails to beat the equal-weight eligible basket under the same BTC filter, or alt-season reversals produce >20% drawdowns.
strategies.author: research-agent
